qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Multi-year government and enterprise IT outsourcing contracts provide baseline switching costs, but CGI faces intense competitive RFP bidding, client rate-card pressure, and limited pricing power unable to consistently outpace tech wage inflation. Primary erosion threats: commoditization of IT implementation and GenAI automated code generation compressing billable hours.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). While CGI possesses switching costs in long-term government and financial IT outsourcing, it lacks structural pricing power above inflation due to competitive RFP rebidding, client rate-card pressure, and exposure to GenAI-driven coding automation compressing billable labor hours.
qualitative.evidence: CGI generates stable ~15-18% GAAP ROIC and >100% FCF conversion via disciplined M&A and outsourcing integration. However, as an IT services provider operating largely on fixed-price and billable-hour contracts, gross margins (~31%) have limited expansion capability against tech wage inflation. IT consulting is structurally exposed to cognitive automation (coding agents) reducing project person-hours, precluding pricing power above inflation.
